<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin="par72" />employed in the sense of {{GHGterm|Piʿēl}} and as a substitute for it, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=קוֹמֵם|translate=to set up}} from {{GHGheb|text=קוּם}}; {{GHGheb|text=מוֹתֵת|translate=to slaughter}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=14|verse=13}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=17|verse=51|hidebook=1}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=1|verse=9}}, from {{GHGheb|text=מוּת}}; {{GHGheb|text=רוֹמֵם|translate=to exalt}}, passive {{GHGheb|text=רוֹמַם}}, from {{GHGheb|text=רוּם}}; reflexive {{GHGheb|text=הִתְעוֹרֵר|translate=to stir up oneself}} (cf. {{GHGheb|text=יִתְעֹרָֽר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=17|verse=8}} in {{GHGterm|pause}}) from {{GHGheb|text=עוּר}}; reciprocal {{GHGheb|text=הִתְבּשֵׁשׁ|translate=to be ashamed before one another}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=2|verse=25}}. The conjugation ''Pilpēl'' ({{GHGpar|55|f}}), on the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}}, is less common, e.g., {{GHGheb|text=טִלְטֵל|translate=to hurl away}} from {{GHGheb|text=טוּל}}; {{GHGheb|text=כִּלְכֵּל|translate=to contain}} from {{GHGheb|text=כּוּל}}; {{GHGheb|text=קַרְקַר|translate=to destroy}} from {{GHGheb|text=קוּר}}.

{{center|{{Small-caps|Remarks}}

I. ''On Qal.''}}

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|n}}
1. Of verbs ''middle e'' and ''o'', in which, as in the strong verb, the {{GHGterm|perfect}} and {{GHGterm|participle}} have the same form ({{GHGpar|50|b}}<!-- the text says 50. 2, but the link is to 50b -->), the following are the only examples: {{GHGheb|text=מֵת|translate=he is dead, fem.}} {{GHGheb|text=מֵ֫תָה}}, 2nd {{GHGterm|masc.}} {{GHGheb|text=מַ֫תָּה}} (cf. {{GHGpar|44|g}}; {{GHGpar|66|h}}); 1st ''sing.'' {{GHGheb|text=מַ֫תִּי}}, {{GHGheb|text=וָמַ֫תִּי}} (even in {{GHGterm|pause}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Gn|chapter=19|verse=19}}); ''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=מֵ֫תוּ}}, 1st ''pers.'' {{GHGheb|text=מַ֫תְנוּ}}, in {{GHGterm|pause}} {{GHGheb|text=מָ֫תְנוּ}}; {{GHGheb|text=בּשׁ|translate=he was ashamed}}, {{GHGheb|text=בּשְׁתְּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=בּ֫שְׁתִּי}}, {{GHGheb|text=בּ֫שְׁנוּ}}, {{GHGheb|text=בּ֫שׁוּ}}; {{GHGheb|text=אוֹר|translate=it has shone, plur.}} {{GHGheb|text=א֫וֹרוּ}}; {{GHGheb|text=טוֹב|translate=to be good}}, {{GHGheb|text=טֹ֫בוּ}}. {{GHGterm|Participles}} {{GHGheb|text=מֵת|translate=a dead man}} (''plur.'' {{GHGheb|text=מֵתִים}}, {{GHGheb|text=מֵתֵי}}); {{GHGheb|text=בּוֹשִׁים|translate=ashamed}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=32|verse=30}}. For {{GHGheb|text=נֵד}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=27|verse=11}} read {{GHGheb|text=נָד}}, or, with LXX, {{GHGheb|text=עַד}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|o}}
Isolated anomalies in the {{GHGterm|perfect}} are: {{GHGheb|text=וְשָׁבַ֫ת}} (with the original ending of the {{GHGterm|fem.}} for {{GHGheb|text=וְשָׁבָ֫ה}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=46|verse=17}} (see {{GHGpar|44|f}}); {{GHGheb|text=צָקוּן}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=26|verse=16}} (see {{GHGpar|44|l}}).—In {{GHGheb|text=בָּ֫נוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 S|chapter=25|verse=8}} (for {{GHGheb|text=בָּאנוּ}} from {{GHGheb|text=בּוֹא}}) the {{GHGheb|text=א}} has been dropped contrary to custom. In {{GHGheb|text=בֹּ֫אוּ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=27|verse=18}} (instead of {{GHGheb|text=בָּ֫אוּ}}) the Masora seems to point to the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=יָבֹא֫וּ}} which is what would be expected; as {{GHGterm|Yôdh}} precedes, it is perhaps simply a scribal error.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|p}}
The form {{GHGheb|text=קָם}} occurs (cf. {{GHGpar|9|b}}) with {{GHGheb|text=א}} in the {{GHGterm|perfect}}, {{GHGheb|text=קָאם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ho|chapter=10|verse=14}}, also in the {{GHGterm|participles}} {{GHGheb|text=לָאט|translate=softly}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=4|verse=21}}, {{GHGheb|text=רָאשׁ|translate=poor}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=12|verse=1.4}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=10|verse=4}}, ''plur.'' {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=13|verse=23|hidebook=1}}; {{GHGheb|text=שָׁאטִים|translate=doing despite unto}} (unless {{GHGheb|text=שֹֽׁאֲטִים}} is to be read, from a stem {{GHGheb|text=שׁאט}} whence {{GHGheb|text=שְׁאָט}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=25|verse=15}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=36|verse=5|hidebook=1}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=28|verse=24.26}}; {{GHGterm|fem.}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=16|verse=57|hidebook=1}}; also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=14|verse=10}} {{GHGheb|text=רָאמָה}} is to be read with Ben-Naphtali for {{GHGheb|text=רָֽאֲמָה}}. On the analogy of participles of verbs ''middle ō'' (like {{GHGheb|text=בּוֹשִׁים}}, see above) {{GHGheb|text=קוֹמִים}} occurs for {{GHGheb|text=קָמִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=16|verse=7}} and even with a transitive meaning {{GHGheb|text=לוֹט|translate=occultans|en=covering}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=25|verse=7}}; {{GHGheb|text=בּוֹסִים}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Zc|chapter=10|verse=5}}.—{{GHGterm|Participle passive}}, {{GHGheb|text=מוּל|translate=circumcised}}; but {{GHGheb|text=סוּג|translate=a backslider}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=14|verse=14}}, and {{GHGheb|text=סוּרָה|translate=put aside}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=49|verse=21}} (cf. {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=17|verse=13}} {{GHGterm|Q<sup>e</sup>rê}}), are verbal adjectives of the form ''qāṭûl'' ({{GHGpar|50|f}}), not passive participles. For {{GHGheb|text=חֻשִׁים|translate=hastening}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=32|verse=17}}, read {{GHGheb|text=חֲמֻשִׁים}} as in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ex|chapter=13|verse=18}}; for {{GHGheb|text=שׁוּבֵי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=2|verse=8}} read {{GHGheb|text=שָׁבֵי}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|q}}
2. Imperfects in ''û'' almost always have the corresponding {{GHGterm|imperative}} and {{GHGterm|infinitive construct}} in ''û'', as {{GHGheb|text=יָקוּם}}, {{GHGterm|imperative}} and {{GHGterm|infinitive}} {{GHGheb|text=קוּם}} (also defectively written {{GHGheb|text=יָקֻם}}, {{GHGheb|text=קֻם}}); but {{GHGheb|text=יָדוּשׁ|translate=he threshes}} (''infin.'' {{GHGheb|text=דּוּשׁ}}), has {{GHGterm|imperative}} {{GHGheb|text=דּ֫וֹשִׁי}} ({{GHGterm|fem.}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=4|verse=13}}; {{GHGheb|text=יָמוּט|translate=it slippeth, infinitive}} {{GHGheb|text=מוֹט}} ({{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=38|verse=17}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=46|verse=3|hidebook=1}}); cf. {{GHGheb|text=נוֹחַ}} (also {{GHGheb|text=נוּחַ}}) {{GHGbible-ref|book=Nu|chapter=11|verse=25}} and {{GHGheb|text=נוֹעַ}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=7|verse=2}} (elsewhere {{GHGheb|text=נוּעַ}}) with the ''imperfects'' {{GHGheb|text=יָנוּחַ}} and {{GHGheb|text=יָנוּעַ}}; {{GHGheb|text=לָעוֹז}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=30|verse=2}}; {{GHGheb|text=שׁוֹב}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jos|chapter=2|verse=16}}; {{GHGheb|text=רוֹם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=10|verse=17}} (verse 16 {{GHGheb|text=רוּם}}).

{{GHGmargin-letter|72|r}}
Where the {{GHGterm|imperfect}} (always intransitive in meaning) has ''ô'' the {{GHGterm|imperative}} and {{GHGterm|infinitive}} also have it; thus {{GHGterm|imperfect}} {{GHGheb|text=(יָבֹא) יָבוֹא}}, ''infin.'' and ''imper.'' {{GHGheb|text=בּוֹא}} or {{GHGheb|text=בֹּא}}<ref>In {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=14|verse=12}} ({{GHGheb|text=בְּבֹאָה}} before a genitive), the text is evidently corrupt: read with Klostermann after the LXX {{GHGheb|text=בְּבֹאֵךְ}}.</ref>; {{GHGheb|text=וַיֵּאֹר}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=2|verse=32}}, {{GHGheb|text=א֫וֹרִי}}, {{GHGheb|text=א֫וֹרוּ}}; {{GHGheb|text=יֵבוֹשׁ}}, {{GHGheb|text=בּוֹשׁ}}, &c.—{{GHGheb|text=יָקוֹט}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=8|verse=14}} (if it be a verb at all and not rather a substantive) is formed on the analogy of verbs {{GHGheb|text=ע״ע}},<section end="par72" /><noinclude>
<references/></noinclude>
